title: InvokeBidi per-direction HMAC chain anchored on Ed25519 envelope signature
description:
RFC 001 §A16 (P5-rewrite-15) introduces the InvokeBidi RPC for bidirectional realtime multimodal sessions. A bidi session is one Invocation governed by the same seven-tuple as Invoke / InvokeStream — no eighth axiom parameter — but its body consists of frames that must be integrity-bound to the signed envelope.

This case pins the four byte-level constants every conforming SDK port MUST reproduce:

  1. HKDF-SHA256 derivation of two per-direction MAC keys from (envelope_signature, invocation_nonce). Salt and per-direction info labels are protocol-versioned.
  2. HMAC-SHA256-32 chain over (sequence_be_8 || prev_mac || canonical_payload_bytes). Frame 1 anchors on the 64-byte Ed25519 envelope signature; frames N≥2 anchor on the previous frame's 32-byte tag.
  3. Canonical bidi-frame encoding: prost deterministic encoding of `InvokeBidiUp` / `InvokeBidiDown` with the `mac` field cleared to empty bytes before encoding. Both producer (caller) and verifier (callee) feed identical bytes into HMAC.
  4. Wedge property: flipping a single byte in any frame N's canonical payload changes every subsequent tag in that direction; frame N-1's tag is unchanged.

binding_constants.v1_ordering: STRICT (case-sensitive; empty string accepted as default)

inputs.invocation_nonce_bytes_recipe: ASCII bytes of "anchor-nonce-fixed" — 18 bytes (the anchor uses a non-16-byte string deliberately to keep the recipe portable across SDKs that may impose tighter nonce-length validation; production envelopes use a 16-byte CSPRNG nonce per RFC 001 §3.2.5)

expected_outputs.rule: up_key MUST NOT equal down_key (different `info` labels). Re-deriving with the same inputs MUST produce the same bytes.

inputs.prev_mac_bytes_recipe: 64 zero bytes (simulating frame-0 Ed25519 signature anchor for frame 1)

wedge_property.rule: For any chain (key, envelope_signature, payloads[]) producing tags[i], flipping one byte in payloads[k] (1-indexed) yields a chain whose tag[k-1] is identical to the original but tags[k..] all differ.
wedge_property.narrative_recipe: (1) Build an honest 4-frame chain from anchor=64×0xAA with payloads=["frame-1","frame-2","frame-3","frame-4"] under key=32×0x55. (2) Build a tampered chain where payloads[1] = "frame-2!" (one byte appended). (3) Assert tags[0] match (frame-1 anchored on the same envelope_signature, payload unchanged) AND tags[i] differ for i ∈ {1,2,3} (the chain wedges every successor).

wire_format_pins.sequence_strict_rule: frame.sequence MUST equal last_seen + 1 exactly; gaps and reorders rejected with AXON_BIDI_FRAME_SEQUENCE
wire_format_pins.stream_id_rule: 0 acceptable iff streams[] empty or contains exactly one descriptor; otherwise stream_id MUST match a declared id (else AXON_BIDI_UNKNOWN_STREAM_ID)
wire_format_pins.ordering_rule: StreamDescriptor.ordering MUST be empty or "STRICT" in v1 (case-sensitive); else AXON_BIDI_NON_STRICT_ORDERING

notes: Confidentiality is intentionally out of scope at the frame layer. Production deployments rely on TLS for confidentiality of `BinaryChunk.data`; per-direction AEAD is reserved for a future amendment if a deployment needs to defend against a compromised TLS terminator.

Loss-tolerant ordering (StreamDescriptor.ordering = "LOSS_TOLERANT") is reserved for a v2 amendment. v1 receivers MUST reject any non-STRICT ordering. PTY and any control-plane stream stay STRICT unconditionally because their frames carry irreversible operations (process input, signals, resize) for which silent loss is unacceptable.

The seven-tuple invariance is preserved: opening InvokeBidi does not introduce an eighth AXIOM parameter. The frame chain is a derived obligation over the existing signed envelope, not a parameter extension.

Every conforming SDK port MUST pass the two per-byte anchor vectors and the wedge-property test exactly. Ports that emit InvokeBidi frames MUST also enforce the wire-format pins (sequence strictness, MAC length, sig-anchor match) and emit one of the listed reason codes on rejection.

consumers.loader_rule: This critical vector is not optional. The listed tests are the release-blocking consumers for the contract pinned here.
